title: XMPP Addressing (RFC 7622): Parsing, Validating & Normalizing JIDs
solutionExplanation:
The solution parses the JID in two stages:
1. binary:split(JidBin, <<"/">>) separates the optional Resource part. If the slash exists but the resource is empty, it returns {error, invalid_jid}.
2. parse_bare splits the bare component on <<"@">>, confirming that both user and domain are non-empty.
3. binary:copy/1 is executed on User, Domain, Resource, and Bare to unpin any references to larger network buffers.
4. to_bare and format_jid handle map and binary representations seamlessly.

mentalModelCheck.question: Under RFC 7622, what is the architectural difference between a Bare JID (user@domain) and a Full JID (user@domain/resource)?

options.label: A Bare JID identifies the user account (for presence subscriptions and roster management), while a Full JID routes to a specific connected client socket session.
options.explanation: Full JIDs include the bound resource identifier and correspond directly to a unique online socket session.

options.label: Bare JIDs are only used on localhost, while Full JIDs are used on the internet.
options.explanation: Bare and Full JIDs are used everywhere across local and federated XMPP architectures.

options.label: Bare JIDs cannot receive chat messages.
options.explanation: Bare JIDs can receive messages; the server routes them to the highest priority connected resource or stores them offline.

options.label: Full JIDs require RSA signatures.
options.explanation: JIDs are simply structured protocol addresses, not cryptographic signatures.
